findings.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — group.users.delete(id)` takes the has_many-:through `delete_all` path, so GroupUser callbacks never run and the `groups.user_count` counter cache is never decremented — spec:129 asserts `group.users.count` (a live COUNT), so this ships green forever.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:14 — Cascade of the stale counter: the admin editor's "Group members (N)" and pager read the live `meta.total` after `findMembers`, while `/admin/groups`, the public group page and every other `BasicGroupSerializer` consumer read the drifted `groups.user_count` column — the two disagree silently after any removal.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — Rails' `CollectionProxy#delete` calls `find(records)` when given a Fixnum, so removing a user who is no longer a member raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` (404) instead of a no-op — trigger: two admins on the same group, or one admin retrying after a timeout, or a stale page-2 roster.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Usernames are not stripped, so an admin who types `alice, bob` in the selector silently loses ` bob` and still gets `success_json`; spec:103 joins with a bare `,` so the suite never sees the whitespace path.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Unknown usernames are dropped with no accumulation and the action returns `success_json` regardless — with N names where the 3rd is a typo, the admin sees success and a roster missing one person, with nothing to distinguish it from a full add.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1` overcounts whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`: a group with exactly 50 members at the default limit 50 reports `totalPages` 2, so "next" stays enabled and lands on an empty page labelled "2/2".

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23 — params[:offset].to_i` is unclamped on a publicly reachable endpoint: `GET /groups/staff/members.json?offset=-1` emits `OFFSET -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects, producing an unhandled 500.

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit` is unclamped: `?limit=-1` gives `LIMIT -1` (PG error, 500) and `?limit=1000000` serializes an entire group's users through `GroupUserSerializer` in one anonymous request.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:67 — params.require(:usernames)` runs before the automatic-group guard and assumes a String — an authorized admin posting `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b` hits `Array#split` and gets a NoMethodError 500; a blank `usernames` gets 400 instead of the intended 422.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:77 — group.add` already commits the GroupUser rows (the old `update_patch` rendered success with no save at all), so the `if group.save` wrapper can return `render_json_error` for membership changes that are already durable — the client, which has no error handler, then shows the pre-add roster.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — No cap on the comma-separated list: one PUT with tens of thousands of names runs that many `find_by_username` lookups plus inserts, unbatched and outside a transaction, so a timeout leaves a half-applied roster and no error the client can act on.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:25 — The member refresh URL keys off `this.get('name')`, which is two-way bound to the unsaved Name text field — edit the name, then page or remove a member, and the refresh hits `/groups/<unsaved-name>/members.json` and 403s, so the roster silently stops updating.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:45 — removeMember` and `addMembers` attach no rejection handler, so the 422 for an automatic group and the 404 from removing an already-removed member both render as "the X button did nothing".

app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:13 — offset` is never reset on route entry and the model is the long-lived object held in the `adminGroups` array, so leaving a group at page 3 and re-entering it reloads page 3 — past the end if members were removed meanwhile.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:33 — next` clamps offset to `user_count` (a count, not a page boundary) and both pagers discard the `findMembers` promise with no in-flight guard, so double-clicking the arrow fires overlapping requests whose out-of-order responses reset `offset`/`members` to the earlier page.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Discourse.Group#removeMember`, after a successful DELETE it only calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting `offset`. If you were on the last page and delete the last member, the model may still have the old `user_count` (e.g., 101) and an `offset` equal to the old last page start (e.g., 100). The next request goes out with `offset=100`, while the new total is 100, so the server returns an empty members list and then sets `offset` to 100, leaving the UI on an empty page. Nothing in the diff clamps offset to a valid page start after deletion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Unknown or misspelled usernames are silently skipped yet add_members still returns success_json, making a wholly failed add indistinguishable from a successful one.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds users when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; otherwise it does nothing (unknown/misspelled usernames are silently ignored). After the loop it calls `group.save` and, if it returns truthy (which it typically will even if no members were added), it returns `success_json`. There is no check that at least one username resolved/was added, so a request where all usernames are invalid is indistinguishable (HTTP 200 + success_json) from a fully successful add.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — usernames.split(",") does not strip whitespace, so "alice, bob" silently drops " bob" because find_by_username misses on the leading space.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, `usernames` is a raw string from params and is processed with `usernames.split(",")`. The resulting tokens are used directly in `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming. If the input is `"alice, bob"`, the second token will be `" bob"` (leading space) and `find_by_username` will not match, so that user won’t be added. This is a concrete correctness issue visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:67 — params.require(:usernames) runs before the automatic-group guard, returning 400 instead of the intended 422; an array-valued usernames param hits Array#split and 500s.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` before `return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic`. If `usernames` is omitted, `params.require` will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` and respond 400, bypassing the intended 422 “can_not_modify_automatic” response for automatic groups. Also, `usernames.split(",")` assumes `usernames` is a String; if the request supplies `usernames` as an Array (e.g., `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), `Array#split` will raise (NoMethodError), resulting in a 500. Both behaviors are directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:23 — offset is not clamped to >= 0, so offset=-1 emits OFFSET -1 and an unhandled PG error, and a non-numeric limit silently becomes LIMIT 0 (looks like an empty group).

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then uses `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. In Ruby, a non-numeric string like "abc" becomes 0 via `.to_i`, yielding `LIMIT 0` (empty result) without any validation. Also "-1" becomes -1, so `.offset(-1)` can generate SQL with `OFFSET -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects (OFFSET must not be negative), raising an exception because there is no clamping/handling in this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — update unconditionally sets visible = (params[:visible] == "true"), so a partial update that omits :visible silently un-publishes the group.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#update, the code sets `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` unconditionally. If a client performs an update that does not include the `visible` param (e.g., only changing `alias_level` or `name`), then `params[:visible]` is nil and the expression evaluates to false, causing the group to be saved as not visible. Other fields in the same method are guarded by `if params[:alias_level].present?` / `if params[:name]`, so the unguarded `visible` assignment would indeed silently change state when omitted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22 — create never reads params[:alias_level] even though asJSON sends it and the form renders the alias-level combo for new groups, so the chosen value is dropped while the client model keeps showing it.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Discourse.Group#asJSON` now sends `{ name, alias_level, visible }`, and the group form (`admin/templates/group.hbs`) renders the alias-level combo-box regardless of whether the group already exists. However, `Admin::GroupsController#create` only sets `group.name` and `group.visible` and never reads/assigns `params[:alias_level]` (unlike `update`, which does set `group.alias_level`). As a result, when creating a new group with a non-default alias level selected, that choice will not be persisted and the server will use the default `alias_level` instead, while the client-side model may still reflect the selected value until a reload.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — findMembers now returns undefined instead of Ember.RSVP.resolve([]) for a nameless group, so any caller chaining .then() will throw.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` was changed to `return;` when the group has no name, instead of returning `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`. That does mean `findMembers()` can return `undefined` in that case. However, all call sites shown in this diff were also changed to no longer chain `.then(...)` (the previous `afterModel` hooks that did so were removed), and the remaining uses simply call `model.findMembers()` or `return group.findMembers()` without chaining. So the specific failure mode claimed (“any caller chaining .then() will throw”) is not demonstrably triggered by the code in this diff; asserting other callers exist outside the diff is speculative.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:30 — Concurrent findMembers calls (rapid next/previous, or a removal racing a page change) can resolve out of order and overwrite members/offset/user_count with a stale response.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In discourse/models/group.js, findMembers() issues an async Discourse.ajax call and, on resolution, unconditionally self.setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members }). The diff introduces multiple call sites that can fire findMembers back-to-back (admin-group controller actions next/previous; removeMember/addMembers call findMembers() after their own ajax; routes call model.findMembers() in setupController without awaiting). There is no request sequencing/cancellation token, so responses can resolve out of order and the later-resolving (stale) response can overwrite members/offset/user_count with older page data, making pagination state incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:1 — {{#if model}} now tests the Group object (always truthy) rather than the members array, so an empty group renders a bare table header instead of nothing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `group/members.hbs` only changes the iteration from `{{#each m in model}}` to `{{#each m in members}}`. Although the route/controller now sets `model` to the Group object (and triggers `model.findMembers()`), the alleged issue hinges on an unchanged `{{#if model}}` behaving differently for empty groups. Previously `model` was an array of members, but in Ember/Handlebars an empty array is still truthy, so `{{#if model}}` would already render the table header even when there were zero members. Therefore, the finding’s claim that this change introduces “header instead of nothing” for empty groups is not a verifiable new defect from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:10 — Default page size 50 is hardcoded in the client model and duplicated again in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22, with no shared constant or site setting.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a hardcoded default limit of 50 in two places: `Discourse.Group` sets `limit: 50` client-side, and `GroupsController#members` defaults `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` server-side. This duplication is verifiable, but it is not a functional bug or correctness/security defect by itself—both sides agree on 50 and the system works. The complaint about lacking a shared constant/site setting is a maintainability preference rather than a clear problem introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23 — Offset clamping lives in findMembers and is re-implemented in the controller's next/previous actions (admin-group.js.es6:33 and :44).

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show offset bounds logic in two places: `Group.findMembers` clamps `offset` (`Math.min(user_count, Math.max(offset, 0))`), while the admin controller’s `next`/`previous` actions also clamp offsets with `Math.min(..., user_count)` / `Math.max(..., 0)`. However, this is duplication/maintainability, not a verifiable defect by itself: the clamping in both places is consistent and doesn’t inherently introduce incorrect behavior. The real correctness risk in this area would be from other logic (e.g., `totalPages` calculation), not from the mere re-implementation of clamping.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:6 — Pagination state is split across the model (limit/offset/user_count) and the controller (currentPage/totalPages/showingFirst/showingLast), so every other consumer of Group must reimplement the page math.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does place pagination *data* (limit/offset/user_count) on the Group model and pagination *UI state/math* (currentPage/totalPages/showingFirst/showingLast) on the admin controller, but this is not a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect. It’s an architectural preference/maintainability suggestion, and the diff does not show any other consumer that is forced to duplicate this logic (the public group-members route simply calls model.findMembers() and does not implement pagination math). A reasonable reviewer could suggest refactoring, but it’s not a clear defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:31 — The raw server envelope (result.meta.total/limit/offset) is written straight onto the client model as snake_case properties, leaking the wire shape into controllers and templates.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the Group model already defines and uses snake_case properties (`user_count`, `limit`, `offset`) and templates/controllers reference them directly (e.g., `user_count` in `admin-group.js.es6` and `group.hbs`). `findMembers` maps the server envelope to these same model properties (`user_count: result.meta.total`, `limit: result.meta.limit`, `offset: result.meta.offset`). This is not a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff; it’s an architectural/style preference about naming and “wire shape” exposure, and the code intentionally normalizes `total` -> `user_count` anyway.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:70 — New instance method named `create` collides conceptually with Ember's `Discourse.Group.create()` factory used at lines 104 and 116, so `create` means two different things in one file.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `create` is added as an *instance* method on `Discourse.Group = Discourse.Model.extend({ ... })` and is invoked on an instance (`group.create()` in the admin controller) to POST the group to the server. Ember/Discourse’s factory method is the *class* method `Discourse.Group.create()` used to instantiate objects; defining an instance method named `create` does not override or break the class method. The proposed finding points to a conceptual naming ambiguity and references usages (“lines 104 and 116”) not shown/verified in this diff, but there’s no verifiable collision/bug introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:67 — add_members identifies users by a comma-joined username string while remove_member uses a numeric user_id, so the two symmetric endpoints use asymmetric identifiers and parsing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows `add_members` expects a comma-separated `usernames` string (splitting it) while `remove_member` expects a numeric `user_id`. However, nothing in the diff indicates these endpoints are intended to be symmetric or that this asymmetry causes incorrect behavior: the JS client matches this design (`addMembers(this.get("usernames"))` and `removeMember` sends `member.get("id")`). This is an API design inconsistency at most, not a verifiable bug/correctness defect introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — Server splits a comma-delimited `usernames` string, making the user-selector's raw input format part of the API contract instead of accepting an array.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then `usernames.split(",")`, which indeed assumes `usernames` is a comma-delimited string. However, nothing in the diff shows this is incorrect or broken: the client-side `addMembers` action passes `this.get("usernames")`, and prior code paths also treated usernames as a comma-joined string (e.g., the controller previously built a comma-joined list from members and sent usernames as a string). The finding is essentially an API design preference (accept array vs. comma-separated string), not a clear defect or verifiable bug introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:24 — create assigns only name/visible while update also assigns alias_level, duplicating and silently diverging the attribute-mapping logic between the two paths.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, `Discourse.Group#create()` (client) POSTs `this.asJSON()` which includes `alias_level` and `visible` (and `name`). But `Admin::GroupsController#create` only assigns `group.name` and `group.visible` and never reads/sets `params[:alias_level]`, while `Admin::GroupsController#update` does set `group.alias_level` from `params[:alias_level]`. This is a real divergence introduced by the change: creating a group will silently ignore any requested `alias_level` and default it (likely to 0), unlike updating.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — findMembers now returns undefined for an unnamed group but a promise otherwise (it previously always returned a promise), so callers cannot chain it reliably.

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js, `findMembers` used to always return a promise: for an empty group name it did `return Ember.RSVP.resolve([]);`. The diff changes that guard to `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }`, which returns `undefined`, while the non-empty path still returns the `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` promise. This makes the method’s return type inconsistent and breaks any caller that does `model.findMembers().then(...)` (which was previously safe).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11 — The findMembers() promise is dropped in setupController, and the identical fire-and-forget idiom is duplicated in admin_group_route.js:13, discarding the loading/error handling afterModel previously provided.
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that findMembers() is asynchronous and its returned promise is not handled/awaited (fire-and-forget) in the controller/route setup, meaning member data may not be available when needed and prior loading/error handling is lost—i.e., a race condition/unhandled async issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6 — Public members list now reads the paginated `members` property but ships no pager, so pagination controls exist only on the admin screen while both consumers share the same paginated model.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the public group members route to set the controller model to the Group and call `model.findMembers()` (which now always requests `/groups/:name/members.json` with `limit`/`offset`, defaulting to `limit: 50`, `offset: 0`). The public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` is updated to iterate `{{#each m in members}}`, which will render only `group.members` populated by that single paginated request. Unlike the admin template, no pagination controls or subsequent `next/previous` actions are added for the public members page, so users beyond the first page (50) will never be shown. Previously, non-automatic groups were not paginated server-side, so this is a behavioral regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:1 — The `{{#if model}}` guard is now always true because model is the Group rather than the member array, leaving a dead and misleading condition.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` changes `setupController` to set the controller `model` to the Group (`controller.set("model", model); model.findMembers();`) instead of setting it to the members array. Meanwhile `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` changes the iteration from `{{#each m in model}}` to `{{#each m in members}}`, implying the members list now comes from a `members` property on the Group. If the template still has a top-level `{{#if model}}` guard at line 1, that condition will now be true whenever the Group model exists (which it will for this route), so it no longer guards against “members not loaded / empty” and is misleading/dead as a guard for rendering members.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:1058 — input#group-users` is dead CSS after the selector id was renamed to `user-selector` in admin/templates/group.hbs:28.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:1055 — .row.groups input[type='text']` (500px) out-specifies the newly added `.groups .form-horizontal input` (350px, line 174), leaving two conflicting width rules for the same field.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:20 — Member list reuses the autocomplete wrapper class `.ac-wrap`, which forces the `!important` overrides at admin_base.scss:465 and :468 and couples the list to user-selector styling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:472 — Pager arrow colors are hardcoded #333/#aaa with `!important` instead of the $primary/scale-color theme variables used everywhere else in this file.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:164 — .badges .form-horizontal` rules are now split between line 164 and line 399, and `.groups` styling is spread across lines 164, 463 and 1054.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/views/group-member.js.es6:3 — New view is resolved as `group-member` but its template is named `group_member`, mixing dash and underscore conventions for the same component.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:94 — Automatic-group tests depend on a hardcoded seeded group id of 1 (also lines 52 and 115) instead of fabricating an automatic group.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The updated spec introduces tests that assume an automatic group exists with primary key `1`, rather than fabricating/creating one in the test. In `context ".update"` it does `xhr :put, :update, id: 1, ...` and then `group = Group.find(1)`. In `context ".add_members"` it does `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, ...` and expects a 422 because it’s automatic. adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:115 — remove_member test issues `xhr :put` while the route and the sibling test at line 125 use DELETE.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In config/routes.rb under the admin/groups resource, `remove_member` is wired to `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, while `put "members"` is for `add_members`. But in spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb (the new `.remove_member` context near the end of the diff), the test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, which does not match the routed verb for that action and would hit the wrong route/action or fail routing. This is a concrete mismatch introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:98 — Coverage for silently skipping unknown usernames was deleted even though admin/groups_controller.rb:72 still implements that behavior.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove a spec that asserted adding a non-existent username “succeeds silently” (in the old PATCH incremental update tests). The new implementation in `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` still silently skips unknown usernames via `if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`. However, the proposed finding is about reduced test coverage, not a verifiable defect/bug introduced in the production code by this diff. Nothing in the diff shows that silently skipping unknown usernames must remain guaranteed behavior, nor does the removal itself break functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:62 — TODO "should clear the input" ships with the feature; `usernames` is never reset after addMembers, so the field keeps stale text.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action sends `this.get("usernames")` to `model.addMembers(...)` but never resets/clears `usernames` afterward. Since the template’s `{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}` is bound to that property, the input will keep showing the previously-entered usernames unless the component clears it internally (not shown in this diff). The inline comment `// TODO: should clear the input` corroborates this missing behavior, so the finding is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:49 — The DELETE/PUT pair on the same `members` path maps to inconsistently named actions (`remove_member` singular vs `add_members` plural).

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the same path segment `members` is intentionally routed to different controller actions based on HTTP verb: `DELETE` to `groups#remove_member` and `PUT` to `groups#add_members`. Both actions exist in Admin::GroupsController (`def add_members`, `def remove_member`) and the frontend model uses matching endpoints with PUT/DELETE to `/admin/groups/:id/members.json`. The singular/plural naming difference is cosmetic and does not create a routing/correctness bug in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — User-controlled `limit` has no upper clamp on this anonymous-accessible endpoint, so `?limit=10000000` against an automatic group (e.g. trust_level_0 = every user) fetches and serializes the entire membership in one request.

adjudication.rationale: In GroupsController#members the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit)` without any maximum bound. A client can pass an extremely large `limit`, and since `limit >= total` effectively returns the full membership, the server will load and serialize that entire set in one response (potential DoS). The endpoint is guarded only by `guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)`; there is no clamp in this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:25 — group.users.count` adds a full COUNT(*) over the group_users/users join on every single page request, doubling DB work per page instead of reading the already-serialized denormalized `user_count`.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `total = group.users.count` and then separately loads the page with `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. That is an extra COUNT query on every members-page request (in addition to the actual members SELECT), whereas the model/serializers already expose a denormalized `user_count` field that could likely be used instead to avoid the extra DB work. This is a verifiable performance regression introduced by the diff (even if not a correctness bug).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:26 — order(:username_lower)` spans the join (group_id on group_users, username_lower on users) so no index can satisfy it, forcing a sort of the group's whole membership per page, and OFFSET is uncapped so deep pages generate and discard everything before them.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes the query to `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. While `offset` is taken directly from params (so it can be arbitrarily large), that is typical OFFSET pagination behavior and was already present before for automatic groups; the diff just applies it to all groups. The stronger claim that ordering “spans the join” such that “no index can satisfy it” and that it therefore “forces a sort of the group's whole membership per page” is not verifiable from this diff (indexes/schema and the exact SQL plan are not shown, and planners can sometimes use indexes to avoid full sorts). Overall the finding relies on speculative database/index behavior rather than a clear defect demonstrated by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:72 — User.find_by_username` inside the loop is a classic N+1 (one SELECT per username) where a single `User.where(username_lower: names)` would do.

adjudication.rationale: In the added Admin::GroupsController#add_members method, the code does `usernames.split(",").each` and calls `User.find_by_username(username)` inside the loop. That results in one SQL query per username (plus the group save), which is a verifiable per-item query pattern introduced by this diff. A single batched lookup (e.g., `User.where(username_lower: names.map(&:downcase))`) would avoid that overhead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — The comma-separated `usernames` list is iterated with no cap on its length, so one request can tie up a worker for an unbounded number of sequential lookups and per-user inserts.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then `usernames.split(",").each` with a `User.find_by_username` and `group.add(user)` per entry. There is no length/count cap, batching, or transaction/timeout protection, so a single request can trigger an arbitrary number of sequential DB lookups and membership additions (even if limited to admins). This behavior is directly present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:47 — removeMember` triggers a full `findMembers()` refetch (page query + server COUNT) after every single removal, so clearing N members costs 2N requests and N COUNTs instead of a local splice.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, `removeMember` performs a DELETE to `/admin/groups/:id/members.json` and then, in the `.then(...)`, unconditionally calls `self.findMembers()`. `findMembers()` issues a GET to `/groups/:name/members.json` with `limit/offset` and the server response includes `meta.total`, which (per `GroupsController#members`) is computed via `total = group.users.count`. Therefore each removal causes (at least) 2 requests: one DELETE + one GET that also triggers a COUNT. Repeating removals N times results in ~2N requests and N COUNTs, which is a verifiable performance inefficiency in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:4 — Group.order(:name)` is rendered with no limit or pagination, serializing every group on the site into one response.

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#index the code builds an unpaginated ActiveRecord relation (`groups = Group.order(:name)` with optional filtering) and then calls `render_serialized(groups, BasicGroupSerializer)`. There is no `limit`/`offset`/pagination applied, so the response will serialize all matching groups in one payload, which is a real scalability/performance concern for sites with many groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:13 — afterModel replaced by fire-and-forget model.findMembers(), so a failed fetch is an unhandled rejection and the member list silently renders empty with no loading state

adjudication.rationale: In admin_group_route.js, the previous implementation returned the promise from afterModel (model.findMembers().then(...)), meaning a failed AJAX request would reject the route's model hook chain and be handled by Ember's route error handling (error substates/logging), and the route could also participate in loading behavior. The new code calls model.findMembers() in setupController without returning/awaiting it. In the updated Group#findMembers it performs Discourse.ajax(...).then(...) with no catch. If that AJAX call rejects, nothing in the route catches or propagates it, so the route will render immediately with members undefined/empty and the failure won't trigger route-level error/loading handling. This matches the finding's core claim (fire-and-forget fetch leading to unhandled rejection and no loading/error state).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6:11 — Same un-awaited model.findMembers() in setupController: fetch errors are never surfaced and the page stays permanently blank

adjudication.rationale: In discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6 the diff removes the afterModel hook that returned model.findMembers() and stored the result, and replaces it with an un-awaited call to model.findMembers() inside setupController. That means the route no longer waits for the members fetch before rendering, and Ember’s normal promise-based error substates for route model hooks won’t be triggered on AJAX failure. Since the template was also changed to iterate {{#each m in members}}, the page will render with members initially undefined/empty and, if the request rejects, nothing sets members and no route-level error handling occurs—leaving the members list blank with the error only potentially appearing as an unhandled promise in the console.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — findMembers returns undefined for an empty name instead of a resolved promise, so any caller chaining .then() throws a TypeError

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` was changed from returning `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` when `name` is empty to `return;` (undefined). However, the diff also removes the in-tree callers that were chaining `.then()` (`afterModel` hooks in `admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6`) and replaces them with fire-and-forget calls (`model.findMembers();`) with no chaining. So while the return-type change is real, the specific claim that callers chaining `.then()` will now throw a `TypeError` is not verifiable from this diff because no such chaining callers remain here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:51 — addMembers has no rejection handler, so a 422/403 from the server (automatic group, bad usernames) is silently swallowed with no UI feedback

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `addMembers` (in `group.js`) returns the promise from `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` without an explicit rejection handler, but the proposed scenario isn’t verifiably a real defect here: (1) the UI does not even show the “Add members” control for automatic groups (`group.hbs` wraps it in `{{#unless automatic}}`), so the 422 path for automatic groups isn’t reachable via this UI; (2) the new server-side `add_members` action does not return 422/403 for “bad usernames” — it silently ignores unknown usernames and still returns success if `group.save` succeeds; (3) whether errors are “silently swallowed” cannot be concluded from this diff because `Discourse.ajax` may have global error handling outside the diff. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40 — removeMember has no rejection handler, so a failed DELETE leaves the member displayed and reports nothing to the admin

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `removeMember` returns `Discourse.ajax(...).then(() => self.findMembers())` without an explicit rejection handler. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:47 — The inner self.findMembers() refresh is not returned, so the outer promise resolves before the reload finishes and reload failures go unhandled

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js, both removeMember and addMembers do `return Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { self.findMembers(); });`. Since the `.then` callback does not `return self.findMembers()` (which itself returns the AJAX promise from `Discourse.ajax`), the promise returned by removeMember/addMembers resolves immediately after starting the reload request, not after it completes. Any failure from the reload request would also not be chained to the outer promise, so it won’t be propagated/handled via the original caller’s promise chain.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:58 — Same un-returned inner self.findMembers() in addMembers: caller sees success before the list is refreshed and refresh errors are lost

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Discourse.Group#addMembers` returns `Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { self.findMembers(); })`. Because the `then` callback does not `return self.findMembers()`, the promise returned by `addMembers` resolves immediately after the PUT succeeds, not after the member list refresh completes. Any rejection from `findMembers()` will not propagate to the caller (it becomes an unchained async operation). This is a concrete, verifiable behavior from the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:59 — Missing semicolon after the addMembers .then(...) block relies on ASI and is fragile under asset concatenation/minification

adjudication.rationale: In `addMembers`, the code ends with `return Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { ... })` followed by the function/property terminator `},`. This is valid JavaScript: the `return` statement is terminated before the closing `}` of the function/object literal, and ASI will insert a semicolon at the statement boundary. There is no subsequent line beginning with `(`, `[`, `+`, etc. that would accidentally continue the expression, so concatenation/minification won’t change semantics here. This is at most a style preference, not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23 — Offset is clamped against the stale user_count, so removing the last member of the final page re-requests an out-of-range offset and renders an empty page with no correction

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group#findMembers` the request `offset` is computed before the AJAX call as `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), this.get("offset"))`. After a deletion (`removeMember`), the model’s `user_count` is still the pre-delete value when `findMembers()` runs, so the clamp can keep an offset that is now beyond the last valid page start. The server-side `GroupsController#members` uses `offset = params[:offset].to_i` with no correction/clamping, so an out-of-range offset returns an empty `members` array. The client then sets `offset` to `result.meta.offset` (the same out-of-range value) and does not adjust it, so the UI can remain on an empty page after removing the last member(s) of the final page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:29 — next does not guard against an in-flight findMembers, so double-clicking issues overlapping requests whose out-of-order responses leave offset and members inconsistent

adjudication.rationale: In admin-group controller, the `next`/`previous` actions immediately mutate `model.offset` and then call `group.findMembers()` with no guard/cancellation/disable while the request is in flight. `Group#findMembers` issues an async `Discourse.ajax(...)` and in its `.then` handler unconditionally sets `user_count`, `limit`, `offset`, and `members` from the response meta. If the user triggers multiple navigations quickly (e.g., double-click `next`), multiple requests with different offsets can be outstanding; if responses resolve out of order, the later-resolving earlier request will overwrite `offset`/`members` with stale data, leaving the UI on the wrong page. This race is directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:40 — previous has the same missing in-flight guard and can interleave paged responses

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, both `actions.next` and `actions.previous` immediately mutate `model.offset` and then call `group.findMembers()` with no loading/in-flight guard. `findMembers()` issues an async `Discourse.ajax(...)` and, on completion, overwrites `user_count/limit/offset/members` via `setProperties(...)`. If a user clicks previous/next rapidly, multiple requests can be in flight and responses can resolve out of order, causing `members`/`offset` to reflect a stale page (interleaved paged responses). There is no request token, cancellation, or button disabling during load in the diff, so this is a real correctness risk introduced/left unhandled here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:64 — addMembers discards the returned promise: no error surfacing, no button disable, and the input is never cleared (TODO line 62) so a second click resubmits the same usernames

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:56 — removeMember discards the promise returned by model.removeMember, so a rejected DELETE is silently ignored

adjudication.rationale: In admin-group.js.es6 the removeMember action calls `self.get("model").removeMember(member);` inside the bootbox.confirm callback and does not return or chain the resulting promise (unlike `next`/`previous` which `return group.findMembers()`). `Discourse.Group#removeMember` returns the `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` promise; if that DELETE request rejects, nothing in the controller observes/handles it, so there is no UI error handling and the failure will not be acted upon by this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:4 — usernames is never reset in the route setupController, so text typed on this singleton controller persists across groups and can be added to the wrong group

adjudication.rationale: In Ember, a route’s controller instance is typically reused (singleton per route). adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6 — Public members list is now capped at the model default limit of 50 with no pagination controls, so members past the first page are silently unreachable

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each` and only calls `group.add(user)` when `User.find_by_username` returns a user; missing usernames are ignored and the action still renders `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — usernames.split(",") raises NoMethodError (500) when usernames is submitted as an array or hash instead of a string

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then immediately calls `usernames.split(",")`. `params.require` only enforces presence, not type: if a client submits `usernames[]=` parameters (array) or a nested structure (hash), Rails will produce an `Array`/`Hash` for `params[:usernames]`, which does not respond to `split`, causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500. The method assumes `usernames` is always a comma-delimited `String`, but that is not guaranteed by the controller code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — The per-user group.add loop is not wrapped in a transaction, so a mid-loop failure leaves the group partially updated

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are iterated and `group.add(user)` is called per user without an explicit transaction. However, the diff provides no evidence that `group.add` can fail mid-loop in a way that would leave a corrupted/incorrect state, nor that atomic all-or-nothing semantics are required here. This is largely speculative, and similar per-user add/remove loops already existed in the previous `update_patch` implementation without transactions. Therefore it is not a clear, verifiable defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:67 — params.require(:usernames) raises ActionController::ParameterMissing on a blank value, returning a non-JSON error body the client cannot parse

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `add_members` does use `params.require(:usernames)`, which will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` if the key is absent (and in many Rails versions also if it’s blank). However, this is a newly introduced endpoint and the client-side code added in the same diff explicitly guards against empty input (`if (Em.isEmpty(this.get("usernames"))) { return; }`), so the normal UI path won’t send a blank value. Also, whether `ParameterMissing` yields a non-JSON error body depends on global exception handling in `Admin::AdminController` / application middleware, which is not shown in the diff, so the claim about “non-JSON error body the client cannot parse” is not verifiable from this change alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — group.users.delete removes the membership row immediately, so if the following group.save fails the caller gets an error while the deletion is already committed

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code executes `group.users.delete(user_id)` before checking `if group.save`. `delete` issues the SQL to remove the join-row immediately (it’s not staged on the `group` object), and there is no transaction/rollback around it. Therefore, if `group.save` returns false for any reason (validations, callbacks, etc.), the action will respond with an error even though the membership deletion has already been persisted. This sequencing/atomicity problem is directly visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — limit is taken unbounded from params, letting a client request an arbitrarily large page and force an expensive query and serialization

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and serializes the results. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — Public members endpoint accepts an uncapped user-controlled limit, so an anonymous caller can dump a whole automatic group (e.g. trust_level_0 = every user) in one request

adjudication.rationale: In app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members, `limit` is taken directly from `params[:limit]` (`limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`) and then used in `group.users...limit(limit)` with no upper bound or server-side cap. Since this is a public (non-admin) endpoint gated only by `guardian.ensure_can_see!(group)`, a caller who can see a group can request an arbitrarily large `limit` to fetch very large member lists in a single request (including large/automatic groups if visible).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:26 — Negative limit/offset params are passed straight to the query, producing LIMIT -1 / OFFSET -1 and an unrescued PG StatementInvalid 500 on a public endpoint

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the new code takes `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and passes them directly into `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no clamp to non-negative values. In PostgreSQL, `OFFSET -1` is invalid and will raise an error (surfacing as `ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid` / 500). Since this is a regular `GroupsController` endpoint (not admin-only) gated only by `ensure_can_see!`, a requester can supply a negative `offset` (and possibly `limit`) and trigger the exception.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — params.require(:usernames) is never type-checked, so usernames[]=a makes .split raise NoMethodError and return a 500 instead of a 400

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then immediately calls `usernames.split(",")`. adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — update unconditionally rewrites visible from params, so any request omitting visible silently sets it false and flips the group's guardian visibility

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — No test for limit/offset edge values: non-numeric limit becomes 0 (empty page), negative offset reaches Postgres as an error, and there is no upper clamp on limit.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` with no validation/clamping. In Ruby, non-numeric strings convert via `.to_i` to `0`, so `limit` can become `0`, yielding an empty result unexpectedly. `offset` can become negative (e.g. "-5".to_i), and that negative value is passed directly into `group.users...offset(offset)`, which can surface as an error at the DB/AR layer (Postgres does not accept negative OFFSET). There is also no upper bound on `limit`, allowing arbitrarily large pages. This behavior is directly verifiable from the changed controller code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:11 — New pagination computed properties ship with no JS unit or acceptance test; `totalPages` is off by one for exact multiples (50 members at limit 50 renders "1/2").

adjudication.rationale: The `totalPages` computed property is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (admin-group.js.es6), which is off by one when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 50/50 => 2 pages, but should be 1). Correct logic would be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with 0 handled separately). The “no JS unit or acceptance test” portion is more of a process suggestion and not itself a verifiable defect from the diff, but the off-by-one pagination bug is directly verifiable in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs:6 — Public group members page now silently truncates to the first 50 members with no pagination controls and no acceptance test covering the regression.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit = (params[:limit] || 50)` and `offset`, whereas previously non-automatic groups returned the full member list (only automatic groups were limited). On the client side, `group-members` route now sets the controller model to the group and calls `model.findMembers()`, which fetches `/groups/:name/members.json` using the model’s default `limit: 50` and `offset: 0` and stores results in `members`. The public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` now iterates `{{#each m in members}}` but no pagination UI/actions are added for the public members page (pagination controls were only added to the admin group template). Net effect: the public members page will show only the first 50 members with no obvious way to navigate to subsequent pages, i.e., silent truncation.
